acs.subtitle: Built-in TR-069 server (GenieACS): panel access, CPE setup and provisioning templates.
acs.panelAccess: NSM administrators only, then GenieACS login
acs.panelHelp: It opens in a new tab. NSM checks that you are an administrator; on first access GenieACS asks to create its own administrator and initial configuration (“init” procedure).
acs.linkHint: Link NSM to GenieACS with “Use built-in GenieACS” to see CPEs in NSM:
acs.guideHelp: Menus can change between models and firmware; TR-069 is mostly found on operator models (ONT XZ/XC, Archer VR/VX, some Archer C with ISP firmware).

cpe.title: On the CPE:
cpe.text: Advanced → System Tools → CWMP Settings (or TR-069): CWMP enabled; ACS URL {{url}}; ACS Username and Password empty for the first test, then set them; Periodic Inform enabled every 300 seconds; Connection Request Username and Password with your own credentials, used by GenieACS to contact the CPE.

network.title: Network:
network.text: the CPE must reach this server on port 7547/TCP. Connection requests (immediate actions from the ACS to the CPE) only work when the CPE is reachable; behind NAT changes apply at the next periodic inform.

templates.title: Templates:
templates.text: install the NSM base provisioning below. On first contact (BOOTSTRAP) and at every inform the CPE sets the inform to every 5 minutes and sends firmware, identity and WAN/PPPoE IP.

verify.title: Check in the ACS panel:
verify.text: the CPE appears in Devices with vendor, model and serial; any errors appear in Faults.

nsm.title: In NSM:
nsm.text: create the TP-Link device with its MAC or serial, open the device's ACS tab and link it to the CPE found in GenieACS.

security.auth: After the first test set CPE authentication in GenieACS: Admin → Config, key cwmp.auth (for example AUTH("acs-user", "long-password")) and the same credentials on every CPE.
security.network: Open port 7547 only towards customer networks and, if the CPE supports it, use HTTPS on the ACS.

acs.templatesHelp: In GenieACS a template is a provision (a script that reads and sets parameters) applied by a preset (when: events and a device condition). The button creates or updates NSM's; you can edit them or add others from the ACS panel.
acs.installed: Templates installed in GenieACS: {{items}}. Find them in the ACS panel under Admin → Provisions and Presets.
acs.notConnected: Link GenieACS first in Integrations → GenieACS (“Use built-in GenieACS” button).
acs.presetText: condition {{condition}}, bootstrap, boot and periodic events → provision {{provision}}
acs.templatesCurrent: NSM templates are up to date (installed {{when}}). NSM updates them by itself after every upgrade.
acs.templatesPending: This NSM version has newer templates than the ones installed {{when}}: NSM installs them within 30 minutes, or press Install now.
acs.templatesAuto: Once installed, NSM keeps these templates up to date by itself after every upgrade.
acs.guideIntro: Each router needs one manual step: turn CWMP on and set the ACS URL. From then on NSP recognises the CPE and monitors it read-only, without changing its configuration.
acs.readonlyTitle: What NSP does and does not touch

readonly.reads: Reads: online/offline state, last contact, model, firmware, IP, CPU, memory, WAN traffic, Wi-Fi clients and DSL line.
readonly.actions: Available actions: reboot, firmware check, diagnostics.
readonly.never: Does not change Wi-Fi, LAN, DHCP, PPPoE or any other router configuration. The only setting it writes is the CWMP inform interval.

uisp.tlsWarning: With TLS verification off the token travels over an unauthenticated channel: use it only temporarily on controlled management networks.
uisp.saved: UISP configuration saved. The token is stored encrypted.
uisp.stateHelp: The test only reads the UISP device list.

deviceExposure.helpExternal: The NSM server checks which management services answer on the device IP: one connection per port, only ports known for this vendor, no full scan.

deviceExposure.forwardsOut: Port forwards to the internal network

acsSnapshot.title: Configuration snapshot
acsSnapshot.help: Archives the CPE's configuration parameters, as the ACS read them, in the Backup tab, where you can open and compare snapshots. Passwords and changing values are left out. Not restorable with one click. Backup policies with the TR-069 option take one automatically when something changed.

refreshState.running: The ACS is reading the configuration object by object: {{done}} of {{objects}} read (round {{round}}). Keep the page open or come back later, then save the snapshot.

refreshState.partial: Configuration read again in part: {{done}} of {{objects}} objects.

acsSnapshot.refreshStarted: The ACS is reading the whole configuration: on a large CPE it takes a few minutes, then save the snapshot.
acsSnapshot.refreshQueued: The CPE did not accept the connection request: the configuration will be read at its next contact.

acsSpeedtest.title: Speed test from the CPE
acsSpeedtest.help: The CPE itself downloads or uploads a {{size}} MB file (TR-143): the result is the speed of the customer's line up to the test server, not of the Wi-Fi. During the test the customer's connection is busy.

settings.title: Speed test of the CPEs
settings.help: By default the CPE downloads and uploads the test file from NSM itself, at the address it uses for the ACS on HTTP port 80, with a link valid 15 minutes for that test only. Set the NSM address if the CPEs reach it elsewhere (for example over HTTPS with a DNS name), or other download and upload URLs to measure towards another server.

cloud.title: Upgrade from TP-Link's cloud
cloud.help: The CPE asks TP-Link's cloud for newer firmware by itself, as in the Online Upgrade box of its web page. NSM reads its answer daily and can start that upgrade: the CPE downloads the image from TP-Link, installs it and reboots.

cloud.neverChecked: Read from the CPE once a day.
cloud.warning: The CPE downloads the image from TP-Link and reboots: the customer is offline for a few minutes. TP-Link firmware usually cannot be downgraded.

lifecycleWeb.title: Lifecycle from the web

acsMigration.subtitle: Bulk-migrate customer CPEs to the integrated ACS by reconfiguring CWMP over the management network.
acsMigration.intro: Enter your routers' management subnet, port and the fleet's shared credentials: NSM reaches each device and sets the target ACS URL. Run a dry run first to see which CPEs are reachable.
acsMigration.applyPending: The TP-Link web-interface CWMP rewrite is in field validation for this firmware: for now only the inventory dry run is available.
acsMigration.formHelp: IPv4 subnets only, at most {{max}} addresses per run. The .0 and .255 addresses and the ACS server are skipped.
acsMigration.credentialsHelp: Credentials are used only during the run and are never stored. A dry run does not need them: no credential is sent to any device.

acsAlerts.title: Alerts of the CPEs
acsAlerts.help: NSM opens an issue in the Action Center, with a notification, when a TR-069 CPE stops contacting the ACS, its WAN is down, the WAN reconnects or the CPE reboots too often, the DSL line degrades or the PON received level falls under the threshold. Issues close by themselves when the problem ends. 0 disables a threshold.

fields.offline: CPE no longer contacting the ACS (three missed periodic Informs)
fields.wan_down: WAN down while the CPE still contacts the ACS (backup line or management network)
fields.dsl_rate_drop_percent: DSL downstream drop against the 7-day median (%)

acsFirmwareAuto.title: Automatic firmware download
acsFirmwareAuto.help: When TP-Link publishes a newer firmware for a model and hardware version you have, NSM downloads the official archive from the Italian site and loads the image into the ACS, once per version. Nothing is installed: each upgrade still needs your confirmation on the device's Firmware tab.

uispFirmware.help: UISP downloads the image and installs it on the device, as with UISP's own Upgrade; NSM follows the upgrade and verifies the new version reported by UISP. The UISP token needs write permission.

firmwareSchedule.title: Scheduled upgrade
firmwareSchedule.help: Choose when to upgrade, for example at night. At that time NSM runs every phase by itself with no further confirmation: check, pre-upgrade backup, approval, download, activation with reboot and version verification. If the device cannot be reached within 2 hours, the upgrade is not run.

firmwareSchedule.confirmMany_one: Schedule the upgrade of {{count}} MikroTik for {{when}}? At that time every phase, reboot included, starts with no further confirmation.
firmwareSchedule.confirmMany_other: Schedule the upgrade of {{count}} MikroTik for {{when}}? At that time every phase, reboot included, starts with no further confirmation.

cambiumBackup.title: Configuration backup (SSH)
cambiumBackup.help: cnMaestro cannot export device configurations, so NSM logs in to the ePMP over SSH, reads the running configuration (config show json) and archives it in the Backup tab, complete and restorable from the ePMP Backup/Restore page. Backup policies with the Cambium option run it on schedule.

cambiumBackup.hostKey: SSH host key {{key}} (remembered at the first backup).

cambiumBackup.ownHelp: Only when this device does not use the shared Cambium credentials.
cambiumBackup.sharedTitle: SSH credentials of the Cambium devices
cambiumBackup.sharedHelp: Used by NSM to back up the configuration of every Cambium ePMP over SSH (cnMaestro cannot export it). A device can have its own credentials on its cnMaestro tab. Stored encrypted; the password is never shown again.

acsPortMapping.title: Port forwarding, DMZ and UPnP
acsPortMapping.help: What the CPE exposes to the Internet, as the ACS last read it (every hour). Monitoring only: nothing is changed from NSM. A change is recorded in the device activity.

acsPortMapping.dmzWarning: DMZ on: every port not forwarded elsewhere reaches {{host}} from the Internet.

ispbillingLinks.title: Devices to assign from ISPBilling
ispbillingLinks.help: For each RADIUS account NSM finds the device (PPPoE user of a MikroTik or of a TR-069 CPE, static IP, caller-id or address of the PPP session on a concentrator in NSM) and compares its customer and site with ISPBilling. Nothing changes until an operator confirms; a device of another customer is never moved by itself.

ispbillingLinks.notImported: The ISPBilling customer of this account is not in NSM yet.

acsRestore.title: Restore on the CPE
acsRestore.intro: Bring some parameters of this snapshot back to the CPE: first see what would change, then choose what to restore.
acsRestore.help: Only the writable parameters whose current value (read now from the ACS) differs from the snapshot. Left out: passwords and keys (not in snapshots), values that change by themselves, the ACS link (ManagementServer) and parameters that start actions (diagnostics, upgrades, resets). NSM sends a single setParameterValues command, then reads the parameters back from the CPE.
acsRestore.skipped: Already equal: {{unchanged}} · no longer on the CPE: {{missing}} · not writable: {{not_writable}} · left out: {{excluded}} · not convertible: {{invalid}}.
acsRestore.nothing: Nothing to restore: the CPE already has the snapshot's values.
acsRestore.noPermission: Restoring needs the permission to change devices.
acsRestore.queued: The CPE did not answer the connection request: the command runs at its next contact.

states.requested: Restore of {{count}} parameters sent to GenieACS ({{when}}): waiting for the CPE to run it.
states.verifying: Parameters written: NSM is reading them back from the CPE to verify them.
states.verified: Restore verified ({{when}}): the CPE reports the {{count}} values of the snapshot.
states.mismatch: Restore done, but the CPE reports different values for these parameters ({{when}}):
states.failed: The CPE refused the restore (fault {{fault}}). The command was deleted from GenieACS with its fault: the CPE's queue is not blocked.
states.unverified: Parameters written, but reading them back from the CPE failed (fault {{fault}}).
states.unconfirmed: The CPE did not run the restore within 30 minutes: the command was deleted from GenieACS.
